headline: One more round of minor coastal flooding hits at Friday morning's high tide, then a breezy, showery Friday gives way to a dry weekend before about a half inch of rain Sunday night into early Monday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Friday brings light rain and scattered showers around New York City as the departing storm's low passes well to the northwest through northern New York, with the best chances north and west of the city. Southwest winds gust 20 to 30 mph through the day. Showers could linger over Long Island and Connecticut into early Friday evening, then skies dry out overnight with southwest winds still a bit gusty. No adverse weather impacts are expected on land beyond the coastal flooding.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday looks dry with gusty west winds that ease Saturday night, and Sunday looks dry and calmer. Rain returns Sunday night as another low tracks from the eastern Great Lakes into northern New England, possibly with a second, smaller low crossing the area; the heaviest rain is most likely in the late-night hours. Expect about a half inch, not enough to cause flooding, with a slight chance of thunder and some gusty winds, though wind impacts look minimal for now. The discussion gives no temperature details.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A few showers may linger Monday morning, with southwest winds gusting around 25 to 30 mph that turn west in the afternoon and northwest Monday night. Tuesday looks dry.

coast: Friday morning's high tide brings one more round of coastal flooding, with widespread minor flooding likely as winds turn southwest; localized moderate flooding in the back bays of Long Island's south shore can't be ruled out but looks less likely than earlier forecasts. Coastal Flood Warnings end at 6 AM, followed by Coastal Flood Advisories from 6 AM until noon to 4 PM Friday depending on location, covering New York City, Long Island, the coastal New Jersey counties near the city and coastal Connecticut. Beach flooding and dune erosion continue through at least Friday morning and possibly into the afternoon, with 8 to 12 foot breaking waves that gradually shrink through the day. On the water, a Gale Warning covers the ocean and a Small Craft Advisory covers the Sound, harbor and bays until 6 AM Saturday, with lingering swell making the entrances to Long Island Sound and New York Harbor rough much of Friday; small craft conditions are likely on the ocean Saturday, conditions settle below advisory levels Sunday, and gales are expected on the ocean again Sunday night into Monday, with a few gale-force gusts possible on the Sound and bays.
watch_for: Friday morning's high tide, especially in the back bays of Long Island's south shore
Timing of Sunday night's rain, with a slight chance of thunder and gusty winds
Gales returning on the ocean Sunday night into Monday
confidence: Forecasters expect no major changes to the coastal flood outlook, are fairly confident in Sunday night's roughly half-inch of rain, and are less certain about wind details with the possible second low Sunday night.
